files.description: Repository contributor instructions and routing to scoped architecture rules.
Agent API documentation retained from the existing Greptile agent-file context. This is API reference material, not contributor instructions.
Existing Paperclip review guidance for PR descriptions, UI evidence, and growth of large source files.
Product requirements and review criteria for harness responsibility, minimal user-facing internals, truthful progress, and human decisions.
Module ownership, justification of shared contract changes, delivery scope, and verification across affected consumers.
Limit feature-map additions to substantial new user capabilities; avoid minor-update churn and keep factual corrections minimal.
Dependency cost, responsiveness, and verification requirements for changed server, adapter, and runner execution paths.
Architecture requirements and review criteria for separating chat channel platform implementations from shared orchestration.
Heartbeat module ownership and review criteria for admission, cancellation, recovery, cleanup, and durable execution evidence.
Snapshot retention requirements for migration generation, rebases, and review; preserve SQL migrations and journal history.
Prevent new idle polling; require event-driven producers, real scheduler deadlines, obligation-based recovery, and lifecycle verification without forcing unrelated legacy migrations.

ACPX provider identity model: provider digests attest upstream releases, the pack contract digest covers Runner source and the shared ACPX layer, and profile versions change only for deliberate resets.
Render cost of UI components and hooks over large collections: no nested scans, stable memo dependencies, and realistic-size tests for changed large-collection paths.

Upgrade safety for persisted run, session, launch, and pack state: state saved by the previous release resumes or fails with a permanent, named code, with old-saved/new-resumed and mid-run deploy tests.
Separation of Telemetry, Observability, and the run log, with the review level each path requires.
Company access checks, actor permissions, activity logging for mutations, and consistent HTTP errors on API routes.
The known instance-wide data (announcement dismissals, publication-ID registry, personal workspace preferences, sidebar company order) and the conditions that keep company boundaries intact.
